For mean comparisons, the t-test is particularly suitable for analysis when the two samples are independent, and the data are normally or lognormally distributed in each sample. For a robust t-test analysis, in addition to the independence and normality requirements previously stated, the samples also need to have equal variances. Similar to many analysis of variance (ANOVA) procedures, t-tests are most robust for balanced data. In the case of mean comparisons, t-tests and many other ANOVA procedures perform best when the sizes of the samples are comparable or equal (SAS Institute, 2013b). While the t-test may not utilize all statistical powers when the samples are unbalanced, an alternative method in SAS for performing ANOVA for unbalanced samples is to use GLM regression (SAS Institute, 2015, July). The GLM method enables the partitioning of the variation in a variable’s values into variation between and within several groups or classes of observations. It uses the method of least squares to fit general linear models. Due to this method, GLMs are a flexible generalization of ordinary linear regression by allowing for response variables that have error distribution models other than a normal distribution.
